scope.summary: swarm_edit_live_pg_conflict_merge_search_and_receipts spawns a bounded live child and reaps it at a hard-coded 24-second wall clock. The child body measures ~23.0s on an idle machine. The margin is roughly 1.4 seconds, so the proof reds on machine load rather than on product behaviour.

measured_not_estimated.child_body_elapsed: The child self-reports elapsed_ms=22582 at T0054 and the harness reports "1 passed; 0 failed; finished in 23.03s" on a quiet machine, writing PROOF_PASS with all 54 gates T0001..T0054 green.
measured_not_estimated.budget: test_e7_swarm_edit_proof.rs:3284 child_deadline = wall_started + Duration::from_secs(24); :3283 hard_deadline = wall_started + Duration::from_secs(30). Both hard-coded. There is no environment override.
measured_not_estimated.margin: Roughly 1.4 seconds, or about 6 percent of the budget.

observed_failures: Two consecutive `cargo test --test test_e7_swarm_edit_proof -- --test-threads=1` runs on 2026-08-13 returned 24 passed / 1 failed, panicking at :3366 "complete MT-043 managed-runtime scenario exceeded 30 seconds and was reaped".
A standalone child run taken while the machine was loaded took 57.43s and died after T0050 with "authoritative live attempt exited before all proof gates passed" - it never reached T0051..T0054.
The same binary, same code, same database, run when the machine was quiet: PROOF_PASS in 23.03s.
defect_detail.why_this_matters_beyond_one_test: The failure mode is INDISTINGUISHABLE at the headline from a real product regression - both read as "24 passed / 1 failed" on the exact test that guards MT-120 attribution. This session lost a cycle to it, and the packet has already been bitten twice by wall-clock budgets: the git history records a 10s deadline red-ing under 51-way parallelism, and the MT-108 sweep found four binaries that only pass at --test-threads=1. A budget that thin is a proof that reports on machine load.
defect_detail.explicitly_not_a_request_to_weaken_the_p: The bound exists so a hung managed-runtime scenario cannot wedge the suite, and that purpose must survive. This MT asks for a budget derived from measured worst case with real headroom, not for the bound to be deleted or quietly raised until the test stops failing.

acceptance_criteria.AC-128-1: The child budget is derived from a MEASURED worst case with stated headroom, and the derivation is recorded in the contract. A number changed with no measurement behind it does not satisfy this.
acceptance_criteria.AC-128-2: A reap must be DISTINGUISHABLE from a product failure without reading source. The reap path must report the observed child elapsed time, the budget it exceeded, and the last gate the child reached, so a future runner can tell a slow machine from a broken product at the headline.
acceptance_criteria.AC-128-3: The bound still fires. Prove it RED: force the child to exceed the budget (e.g. an injected stall behind a test-only env var) and show the reap path triggers and cleans up. A budget that can no longer fire is a deleted guard, not a widened one.
acceptance_criteria.AC-128-4: `cargo test --manifest-path src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml --test test_e7_swarm_edit_proof -- --test-threads=1` returns 25 passed / 0 failed on a machine carrying concurrent build load, not only on an idle one.
acceptance_criteria.AC-128-5: No product source is touched. git diff HEAD for src/frontend/handshake_native/src/** and src/backend/** is empty for this MT.

proof_targets.PT-128-1: test_e7_swarm_edit_proof - 25 passed / 0 failed under concurrent load.
proof_targets.PT-128-2: The forced-stall RED run for AC-128-3, with its output retained.

scope.risk_if_missed: MT-120 and every future change guarded by this suite become unverifiable on a working machine: the proof reds for reasons unrelated to the code under test, and the honest response - re-run until quiet - is exactly the habit that hides a real regression.

lifecycle.pivot_impact_2026_08_16: PIVOT IMPACT 2026-08-16: the defect this microtask fixes SURVIVES the SurrealDB pivot and the work remains valid. The problem is a wall-clock MARGIN, not a database: the proof spawns a bounded live child reaped at a hard-coded 24-second budget while the child body measures about 23.0s on an idle machine, so roughly 1.4s of headroom makes the proof go red on machine load rather than on product behaviour. Do not simply raise the constant: measure first, then justify the margin.
